body_text:
The First Isomorphism Theorem for Vector Spaces. For any linear
map $T : V \to W$, the induced mapping
$\widetilde{T} : V / \ker(T) \to \operatorname{im}(T)$ defined by
$\widetilde{T}(v + \ker T) = T(v)$ is a well-defined vector space
isomorphism: $$ V / \ker(T) \cong \operatorname{im}(T). $$ The
quotient removes precisely the directions collapsed by $T$,
leaving a faithful copy of the image. Equating dimensions on both
sides immediately recovers the Rank-Nullity Theorem:
$\dim(V) - \dim(\ker T) = \dim(\operatorname{im} T)$.
